reasoning: Merged the two overlapping proposals to broaden the bare-list rule into one instruction covering named entities and their context-supported shared relations. Kept the distinct name-form refinement as a replacement, since it clarifies when a conventional name includes an apparent category word versus when an added suffix or formal title is redundant.

edits.target: When a prompt consists only of a list of character names or roles, use context to identify their shared work or program if that is the implied target. Return the work or program, not the performers, unless the prompt asks for the cast.
edits.content: When a prompt consists only of a list of named entities, treat it as an elliptical clue to their shared contextual relationship or category when that is implied. Infer the link most strongly supported by context—for example, a shared work or program for fictional characters, or a shared country, institution, office, or affiliation for real people. Return that shared target rather than repeating the list, naming one listed person, or giving an incidental relationship. Do not guess when context supports no common relation.

edits.target: When choosing a name form, distinguish identity-bearing parts from generic type words supplied by the clue. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name; omit a generic label such as an entity type or location type when the clue supplies that type and the shorter name identifies the answer unambiguously.
edits.content: Use the conventional answer form that fits the requested slot. Do not drop a word merely because it resembles a category label if it is part of the entity's conventional name. Conversely, when the clue supplies the category and asks for a nickname, brand, or other bare name, do not add a redundant class suffix or expand it to a formal company or adaptation title. Avoid narrowing a general target to a subtype unless the clue or context requires it. Retain conventional initials that belong to a person's identifying name.
